record.title: Frontier language models rank small-molecule conformers above UFF but below MMFF94
record.summary: Semakin et al. test whether language models can rank molecular conformers from 3D coordinates using relative-energy labels. Their benchmark covers 810 geometries from 27 small molecules. Table 1 reports GPT-6 Astra at mean reliable-pair Kendall τ 0.67 and Claude Opus 5 at 0.61, above UFF (0.23) but below MMFF94 (0.93) and GFN-FF (0.72). The result is a bounded author-run preprint benchmark, not evidence that language models replace molecular mechanics or generalize across chemical space.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors evaluate frontier language models on 810 conformer geometries from 27 small organic molecules, using DFT-derived relative energies and three shuffled prompt orders; the scoring set retains reliable conformer pairs with energy separation of at least 2 kcal/mol.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In Table 1, mean reliable-pair Kendall τ is 0.67 for GPT-6 Astra and 0.61 for Claude Opus 5, above UFF at 0.23 but below MMFF94 at 0.93; GFN-FF scores 0.72. These are author-reported results from the stated benchmark.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report stronger model performance on structures with well-defined hydrogen-bond interactions and persistent difficulty on many ring-strain and torsion-dominated cases; the result does not establish general 3D physical understanding or experimentally useful molecular design.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The authors publicly provide benchmark data, raw inputs, precomputed responses and plotting/reproduction code; reproducing model calls requires the documented dependencies and access to relevant model APIs.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of the reported conformer rankings was located or run.
The benchmark is limited to 27 mostly small molecules and does not establish transfer to larger or chemically diverse scaffolds.
The single-response-per-model-per-molecule design and API/model-specific sampling settings limit uncertainty estimates and strict cross-model comparability.
The ranking task does not establish accurate energies, experimentally validated structures or utility in molecular design.

brief.importance_rationale: If replicated beyond the small-molecule benchmark, coordinate-only conformer ranking by language models could affect how AI chemistry systems combine learned models and force fields. In the reported regime the strongest LLMs remain below MMFF94, so the result is notable evidence of a narrow capability rather than a replacement for computational chemistry.
limitations: This is an author-run preprint benchmark; no independent reproduction was found or performed in this review.
The sample contains only 27 molecules, mostly small QM9 structures, with a restricted conformer-ranking task; broader chemical-space generalization is unmeasured.
Only three prompt-order shuffles and one response per model per molecule are reported; API sampling settings vary by provider.
Kendall τ ranking agreement is not an energy-error measure and does not establish molecular design or experimental utility.
Cross-model correlations with release date and API cost are descriptive; model families and benchmark observations are not independent samples.
brief.summary: Semakin et al. test whether language models can rank molecular conformers from 3D coordinates using relative-energy labels. Their benchmark covers 810 geometries from 27 small molecules. Table 1 reports GPT-6 Astra at mean reliable-pair Kendall τ 0.67 and Claude Opus 5 at 0.61, above UFF (0.23) but below MMFF94 (0.93) and GFN-FF (0.72). The result is a bounded author-run preprint benchmark, not evidence that language models replace molecular mechanics or generalize across chemical space.

technical.claimed_result: Across 27 molecules, 810 geometries and three prompt-order shuffles, the paper reports mean reliable-pair Kendall τ of 0.67 for GPT-6 Astra, 0.61 for Claude Opus 5, 0.23 for UFF, 0.72 for GFN-FF and 0.93 for MMFF94. These are paper-reported benchmark scores; no independent run was conducted here.
technical.compute_or_cost: The paper reports API experiment costs and an association between cost and score, but this review did not audit invoices or recompute cost. The cross-model comparisons are descriptive and model-family observations are not independent.
technical.demonstrated_result: The paper documents its molecule set, reference-energy protocol, coordinate presentation, pair filtering and reported rankings. Its repository exposes data and precomputed responses. This supports the existence of a reproducible benchmark artifact, not independent confirmation of the model results.
technical.mechanism: The benchmark presents rotated Cartesian coordinates and asks language models to rank conformers by relative stability. Reference labels use r2SCAN-3c calculations; ten molecules receive higher-level checks against DLPNO-CCSD(T). The analysis scores reliable conformer pairs and compares model rankings with classical force fields.
technical.regime: 27 small organic molecules: 25 GEOM-QM9 molecules with up to 9 heavy atoms plus two out-of-distribution controls; 30 conformers per molecule (810 geometries). Scoring uses reliable pairs with |ΔE| ≥ 2 kcal/mol and at least 15 such pairs per molecule. Three independently shuffled prompt orders are used.
technical.reproducibility: Authors provide data, raw inputs, precomputed responses and plotting code. No independent reproduction was found in a bounded exact-title/arXiv-ID search; no model calls or code were run in this review. API availability and model snapshot changes may affect reruns.
technical.strongest_baseline: MMFF94 (mean reliable-pair Kendall τ 0.93), with GFN-FF at 0.72; strongest reported language-model scores are GPT-6 Astra 0.67 and Claude Opus 5 0.61.

brief.title: Frontier language models rank small-molecule conformers above UFF but below MMFF94
brief.why_it_matters: A language model’s ability to rank some small-molecule conformers from coordinates could inform hybrid AI chemistry workflows. The comparison also places the capability in context: in this benchmark, the best tested models trail established force-field baselines, and the 27-molecule regime does not test broad chemical generalization.
